messages:
jamie: Heads up — running long streaming-chat + tool-loop workloads and I see steady linear mem growth over ~2h. Heap shows KV pages climbing from ~1.2GB -> 3.8GB. Eviction counters tick but free-list doesn't shrink. Dump excerpt below, attaching full heap/profile to the thread. Anyone seen pages not being coalesced/reused?

arun: can you paste `kvstat --summarize` and the short perf profile? small snippets help triage quickly.

jamie: sure, here's the summarize and a quick sample from perf top during the tail of the run:
```
KV summary: total_pages=4823 used_pages=3621 free_pages=1202 page_frag_pct=37.1 active_large_keys=48
evictions: triggered=1192 reclaimed=1187 reuse_attempts=1187 reuse_success=723
Perf (top): 30% kv_page_coalesce 18% kv_lookup 12% slab_alloc 8% memcpy
```

maria: interesting — reuse_success << reuse_attempts, so something is failing during reuse and pages end up on freelist but not coalesced back into larger spans? could be a partial-write path that leaves holes. Any pattern in key sizes?

jamie: most keys are small-ish (300-1k) but we do have repeated large tool-loop payloads (~80k) intermittently. The sequences are: stream append -> tool-run (writes temp large blobs) -> truncation of temp keys. The large blobs show up as many small allocated slab fragments in the heap profile.

kai: two quick hypotheses: 1) freelist coalescer is not running for pages that were split for large allocations (edge case in page-split code). 2) reuse path does a size-check and rejects slightly-mismatched pages, leaving them stranded. I can instrument `kv_reuse_attempt()` to log mismatch reasons.

arun: +1 to instrumenting. Also add a metric for "page_coalesce_ops" and "page_coalesce_failed_reason". If coalesce fails often we can correlate with the tool-loop pattern.

jamie: I've kicked off a repro harness (local) with a condensed version of the workload — streaming chat + periodic tool-run creating 80k blobs then deleting them. Repro: 10k sessions synthetic -> mem growth visible after ~1500 sessions. Will push the harness and profile to the thread.

maria: if repro is consistent, try toggling `coalesce_window_ms` to a larger value (e.g., 2000ms -> 10000ms) to see if delayed coalescing reduces fragmentation. Also try forcing a full freelist sweep after tool-run to see if pages get reclaimed.

jamie: quick experiment: forcing sweep at intervals reduces peak by ~30% but doesn't eliminate drift. So some pages are still being retained. Heap shows refs from `message_cache` and `session_journal` during the peak but those refs look stale (should be freed).

kai: could be double-path ownership: temp large blobs move pointers between journal and cache during commit. If free happens on the wrong path we may leak the page header. Instrumenting will confirm.

arun: ops: 1) instrument reuse failure reasons 2) add page_coalesce metrics 3) run repro for 10k sessions and collect heap diff 4) verify no background GC/last-minute retention by other subsystems 5) if confirmed, prepare a small patch to coalesce on free path.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: topic=kv-instr, env=staging, user=jamie, status=queued :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: also add an E2E that simulates intermittent large writes interleaved with small frequent writes. That pattern seems to amplify fragmentation.

jamie: thanks — will post repro logs and instrumented traces when ready. For now marking thread as investigating. :mag:
